Maine Snowmobile Association Testimony in Opposition to LD 1565
An Act to Allow the Use of Certain All-terrain Vehicles on Snowmobile Trails April 23, 2025
Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts, and members of the committee, my name is Al Swett and I am
here today on behalf of the I\/laine Snowmobile Association to testify in opposition to LD 1565.
The I\/laine Snowmobile Association is comprised of 280 member clubs in every corner of l\/laine-- and thousandsof volunteers who spend their blood, sweat, and tears maintaining more than 14,000 miles of
snowmobile trails statewide for the enjoyment of residents and visitors alike.
LD 1565 would amend Title 12, Subsection 13107 to allow owners of all terrain vehicles equipped with tracks to purchase an endorsement sticker for $25 which would permit them to ride on trails that are financed with money from the Snowmobile Trail Fund.
The I\/laine Snowmobile Association opposes this legislation for three reasons:
Safety- Encouraging more ATV's & SxS's onto the trails for this lower fee will increase the concerns
already raised about these machines mixed with snowmobiles on trails that range from 6 to 10ft wide.
Some ATVs equipped with tracks can far exceed the width of snowmobiles and thus trails were not designed for these machines. This poses a danger notjust to passengers in the ATV, but oncoming
snowmobilers as well.
Lack of Clarity- The bill does not specify where the $25 for endorsement sticker will be deposited or how
it will be used.
Financial lmpact- Ironically, MSA is also testifying on another bill (LD 1547) in the Taxation Committee
today. LD 1547 seeks to direct more funding to the Snowmobile Trail Fund, whereas LD 1565 would likely reduce funding and undermines current funding objectives.
Changes to snowmobile registration fees and registration requirements may be necessary in the future,
but they should be based on long-term planning and funding needs and have express support from those that are responsible for maintaining these snowmobile trail systems.
MSA is always happy to engage in discussion with stakeholders, but we believe that this legislation lacks
appropriate safety and financial consideration and would urge the committee to vote ought not to pass.
'
Thank you for your consideration.

Testimony ofRep. Benjamin Hymes on
LD 1565, "An Act to Allow the Use of Certain All-terrain
Vehicles on Snowmobile Trails" Joint Standing Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlifie

April 23, 2025
Good Afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts, and distinguished members
of the Joint Standing Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlife. I am Representative
Benjamin Hymes and I proudly serve House District 38. I am here today to present LD
1565, "An Act to Allow the Use of Certain All-terrain Vehicles on Snowmobile
Trails" .
Currently, ATV owners need to re-register their vehicle whenever they switch between
standard wheels and tracks. They also need to re-register when they switch back. The requirement to re-register every time the owners change their wheels seems like an undo
administrative burden.
My proposal is to give the owners a much more manageable choice. If you own an ATV
and want to keep the standard wheels on, you register in the normal way. If you want to be able to switch between wheels and tracks at your leisure, you can purchase an additional "endorsement sticker" to add to your registration. At the same time, if you want to leave tracks on year-round, you can register as a snowmobile.
I propose a name change to this bill as the title infers that we are changing what types of
vehicles can go on a snowmobile trail. That is not the case. We are changing the registration procedures for ATVs. I recommend something like "An Act to Amend the
Registration Criteria for Certain All-terrain Vehicles."
The $25 price for the endorsement sticker merely a suggestion. If the committee determines the fee should be higher or lower I would be open to having that discussion.
Thank you for your time. I would be happy to answer any questions.
Benjamin C. Hymes
State Representative

Testimony in Opposition to LD 1565 An Act to Allow the Use of Certain All-terrain Vehicles on Snowmobile Trails
April 23, 2025
Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts, and members of the committee, my name is Matt Stedman from Ashland Maine and I am writing today to testify in opposition to LD 1565. The Maine Snowmobile Association is comprised of 280 member clubs in every corner of Maine-- and thousands of volunteers who over 100,000 hrs/season maintaining more than 14,000 miles of snowmobile trails statewide for the enjoyment of residents and visitors alike. As the Maine Snowmobile Association Exec VP, an avid snowmobiler, club volunteer and groomer operator I believe having ATV's and side-by-side's with tracks on snowmobile trails would negatively impact the trails. If these machines want to use the trails, they should have to pay, just like a snowmobile does, to ride the snowmobile trails. Costs' keep going up, why should there be use of the trails without having to pay? There is already a well established system for these tracked ATV's to register as a snowmobile. LD 1565 would amend Title 12, Subsection 13107 to allow owners of all-terrain vehicles equipped with tracks to purchase an endorsement sticker for $25 which would permit them to ride on trails that are financed with money from the Snowmobile Trail Fund. The Maine Snowmobile Association opposes this legislation for three reasons: Safety- Encouraging more ATV's & SxS's onto the trails for this lower fee will increase the concerns already raised about these machines mixed with snowmobiles on trails that range from 6 to 10ft wide. Some ATVs equipped with tracks can far exceed the width of snowmobiles and trails were not designed for them. This poses a danger not just to passengers in the ATV, but oncoming snowmobilers as well. Lack of Clarity- The bill does not specify where the $25 for endorsement sticker will be deposited or how it will be used. Financial Impact- Ironically, MSA is also testifying on another bill (LD 1547) in the Taxation Committee today. LD 1547 seeks to direct more funding to the Snowmobile Trail Fund, whereas LD 1565 would likely reduce funding and undermines current funding objectives. I urge the committee to vote ought not to pass. Thank you for your consideration.
Matt Stedman

TESTIMONY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
IN OPPOSITION TO L.D. 1565
"An Act to Allow the Use of Certain All-terrain Vehicles on Snowmobile
Trails."
PRESENTED BY: Representative HYMES of Waldo
CO-SPONSORED BY: Representative GUERRETTE of Caribou
DATE OF HEARING: Wednesday, April 23, 2025
Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Inland
Fisheries and Wildlife Committee. I am Timothy Peabody, Deputy Commissioner at the
Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, speaking on behalf of the Department, in opposition to L.D. 1565.
This bill provides that when registering an all-terrain vehicle (ATV), a person may
purchase an endorsement for $25 that allows them to switch between tires and snow tracks for the registration period to operate on snowmobile trails in the State. The endorsement is in the form of stickers, which must be displayed on the front and back of the ATV.
\7Vhile it appears this is an attempt to simplify and reduce the cost for an ATV operator to be able to register their ATV one time a year and ride both with tires on ATV trails and
then switch to tracks and ride in the winter, as written we have significant concerns.
For background information when you put tracks on an ATV in the winter it meets the
definition of a snowmobile which allows it to be registered and ridden on statemaintained snowmobile trails, and other private and public lands within the state. This bill would eliminate the requirement to get a separate snowmobile registration by adding
a $25.00 endorsement sticker to an existing ATV registration to allow the machine to be
operated as a snowmobile.
The primary concern of our Department and the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry Off--Road Vehicle Division is the loss of revenue. If passed as written, a
Maine resident would pay $95 to register their tracked ATV as an ATV and a

snowmobile for that registration year, which is a revenue loss of $30.00 per resident dual
registration. A nonresident with the same scenario would pay $140.00 for a full season
ATV registration and a full season snowmobile registration, which is a revenue loss of
$94.00 per nonresident dual registration. Our records indicate that there are roughly 300 -
400 tracked ATVs registered both as an ATV and a snowmobile each year.

application of the endorsement to 3-day and l0-day non-resident registrations. Additionally, the Department will have an additional fiscal impact for programming the
